$comment: Rules enforced by scripts/check-rule-promotion.mjs — the tripwire that
keeps a finished lint migration finished. Each listed rule must resolve
to 'error' severity for every service under services/*/*; a service
where the rule drops to 'warn'/'off'/unconfigured (and still lints
clean) fails the gate. Today that severity lives in the eslint.config.js
base config, so the gate only ever fires if someone downgrades or
scope-exceptions the rule — exactly the drift it exists to catch.
Entry shape:
id               — the ESLint rule id (required)
ratchet          — path to a lint-warning-ratchet baseline for this rule
(optional). Registers the rule with
check-lint-warning-ratchet.mjs as a per-rule
regression floor. For a fully-gated rule the
baseline sits at total 0 and acts as a canary: the
rule is 'error', so any warning that ever appears
means the severity regressed somewhere — and the
zero floor fails CI immediately.
exemptWorkspaces — workspace names that lint clean but must NOT be
forced to 'error' (optional). Each exemption is a
committed decision — the gate warns if one rots.
To migrate a NEW rule with this machinery (the flow require-map-and-throw
used): implement it, set it 'warn' repo-wide, add an entry here with a
ratchet path, and generate the baseline with
`pnpm run check:lint-ratchet -- --update`. Both gates then enforce the
migration (warnings may only decrease; clean services must reach
'error'); when the last service converts, flip the rule to 'error' in
the base config and empty the baseline with one more --update.
Option-level campaigns work on an ALREADY-GATED rule too (the flow
banPlainErrors used on require-map-and-throw): add the option at 'error'
in the base config — if conversion debt exists, warn-block ONLY the debt
surfaces in eslint.config.js (repeating the options; flat config replaces
the whole entry) and --update baselines those warnings under this rule's
id. The per-service completion canary in scripts/__tests__/ keeps the
already-converted semantics at 'error'. If the debt is fully resolved
before the floor is ever written, no warn block and no nonzero baseline
are needed — the option simply goes live at 'error' (enforcement is then
the lint failure itself, with the zero canary guarding the severity).
The gate fails with exit 2 if a listed rule is not configured anywhere for
services — usually a typo in the id. AZEEBO_LINT_RULE=<id> runs the gate
for a single listed rule; an unlisted value is an operator error (exit 2).
